one_line: Prince Santivarma of the Kadamba dynasty, patron of the Talagunda pillar, standing at the cusp of the Triparvatha–Banavasi split in 5th-century Karnataka.

appearance.age_look: mid-20s, athletic but not bulky, with a poised princely bearing
appearance.face: oval face with a straight nose, medium-brown Deccan complexion, sharp arched eyebrows, large anime-style dark brown eyes, a neatly trimmed short moustache, and a calm, thoughtful default expression that hints at political calculation under pressure
appearance.hair: thick black hair tied into a high rounded topknot (similar to early Deccan karnakunda style) wrapped with a narrow gold band, with the sides combed back smooth and a few controlled strands by the temples; no turban or helmet, only a simple tilaka mark on the forehead
appearance.costume: A mid-5th-century Deccan royal outfit: knee-length off-white cotton angavastra-style tunic with short sleeves and a round neck, its borders woven with thin maroon and gold bands; over it, a rich deep-green silk uttariya draped diagonally from the left shoulder across the torso and around the back, fastened at the right hip; lower body clad in a mustard-gold dhoti tightly wrapped and pleated, reaching the ankles and bordered with a narrow maroon stripe; a plain brown leather belt with a simple bronze buckle secures the waist; simple brown leather sandals on the feet; jewellery kept princely but not ostentatious—medium-sized gold karnakunda-style ear ornaments, a single flat gold torque necklace, two slim gold bangles on each wrist, and an armlet on the right upper arm shaped like a subtle coiled serpent motif; no crown, but three small circular gold medallions sewn along the front border of the green uttariya near the left shoulder, alluding to the ‘three crowns’ described in the inscription.
appearance.signature: A sheathed early Indian iron sword with a straight single-edged blade and simple cross-guard, carried at his left hip in a plain brown leather scabbard with modest bronze fittings, which he rests his right hand on when standing in a decisive pose.

ref_desc: Santivarma Kadamba is a mid-20s medium-brown Deccan prince with a high black topknot, tilaka, off-white tunic, deep-green uttariya with three gold medallions, mustard-gold dhoti, simple gold jewellery, brown sandals, and a plain sheathed iron sword at his left hip.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style model sheet of Santivarma Kadamba, a mid-5th-century South Indian prince from the Deccan: he is in his mid-20s, athletic but not bulky, with an oval face, medium-brown complexion, large dark brown anime eyes, a straight nose, sharp eyebrows, and a neat short moustache, wearing a calm, thoughtful expression; his thick black hair is pulled into a high rounded topknot wrapped with a narrow gold band, sides combed back smooth, with a small tilaka on his forehead. Dress him in an era-accurate royal outfit: a knee-length off-white cotton tunic with short sleeves and a round neck, edged in thin maroon and gold borders; over this, a rich deep-green silk uttariya draped diagonally from the left shoulder across the chest and around the back, pinned near the right hip, and on the front edge near his left shoulder three small circular gold medallions sewn in a vertical line; his lower garment is a mustard-gold dhoti wrapped tightly with neat front pleats and reaching the ankles, finished with a narrow maroon border. Add a plain brown leather belt with a simple bronze buckle at the waist, brown leather sandals on his feet, a flat gold torque necklace at the neck, medium-sized traditional gold ear ornaments, two slim gold bangles on each wrist, and a single coiled-serpent gold armlet on his right upper arm. At his left hip, he carries a sheathed early Indian iron sword with a straight single-edged blade and simple cross-guard, in a plain brown leather scabbard with modest bronze fittings, and his right hand often rests lightly on the hilt in decisive poses. Show front, side, and back views using a consistent palette of deep green, mustard gold, off-white, maroon, and medium-brown tones, emphasising historical South Indian draped garments and modest, dignified royal bearing.
